title: BlueHarbor Energy on-prem capacity constraints and TF module review
body:
Executive summary:

This draft captures the current state of the BlueHarbor Energy private deployment engagement: proposed capacity envelope, network/topology constraints discovered during the January site assessment, recommended Terraform module adjustments, and a phased upgrade/rollout plan. It is intended for review by BlueHarbor infra, Redwood Solutions Eng, and internal product owners. Not final — open questions and assumptions are highlighted.

Goals and decision criteria:
- Match 99th percentile latency targets for inference (<=150ms p99 for 512-token sequences) under expected peak concurrent sessions of 120.
- Keep steady-state monthly cost within BlueHarbor procurement target: target cost envelope marked in procurement deck (linked).
- Provide clear upgrade path for future 4x throughput increase with minimal downtime for edge sites.

Site constraints discovered (from on-site Feb 2025 assessment):
- Rack power: two of five designated racks are limited to single 32A PDUs; peak power budget per rack currently ~6.5kW.
- Network fabric: edge site uses two 10Gb LACP uplinks to an MPLS termination; no existing L3 EVPN overlay. Latency to central DC measured at 12-18ms.
- Cooling: CRAC can sustain continuous ~18kW but with +2C ambient at peak summer load.
- Security: HA proxy appliance handles north-south TLS; customer requires HSM integration for KMS but will only provision HSM after contractual amendment (Q2).

Sizing assumptions (working):
- Workload: 60% conversational chat, 40% document summarization. Median prompt length 180 tokens, generated output average 120 tokens.
- Model: they expect to run a quantized 13B model variant with KV-cache support and a smaller 7B fallback for surge.
- Performance profile (expected): 13B q4_0 on A100-80GB equiv: ~45 tokens/sec per GPU for our runtime with current kernel set; 7B q4_0 ~110 tokens/sec. These are conservative figures (see linked benchmark sheet).

Preliminary capacity plan (steady-state to meet p99 target):
- Primary pool: 4x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (spread across 2 racks for power/distribution), serving as main capacity for 13B model.
- Burst/fallback pool: 3x A40/80GB-class GPUs for 7B fallback and unpredictable burst.
- Dedicated KV cache nodes: 2 lightweight VMs (CPU-bound) for prefix caching and fast cold-starts, colocated with primary pool via top-of-rack VLAN.
- Observability/control plane: 2 VM replicas for the private control plane, HA across racks.
- Notes: Given power constraints, we recommend a mix of 2x full-power GPUs per heavy rack and smaller accelerators in the lower-powered racks.

Terraform module recommendations (priority order):
1) modularize gpu_pool resource into three discrete modules: primary_pool, fallback_pool, and cache_nodes. Rationale: simplifies constrained power placement and per-pool autoscaling policy.
2) add placement_constraints variable to each GPU module with allowed_rack_tags list and max_pdu_draw argument. This will allow TF to produce rack-aware placement plans without manual edits.
3) introduce an optional hsm_integration module stub that composes KMS config, provider credentials, and stubbed acceptance tests. Keep it opt-in until BlueHarbor proves HSM availability.
4) add lifecycle.ignore_changes for runtime_kernel_version until we have a stable upgrade window — prevents TF from trying to force kernel swaps during rollout.

Terraform snippets to include in upstream repo (outline):
- variable "placement_constraints" { type = list(string) default = [] }
- module "primary_pool" { source = "../modules/gpu_pool" count = var.primary_count placement_constraints = var.primary_allowed_racks }
- resource "null_resource" "verify_pdu" { provisioner = local-exec when = create command = "scripts/check-pdu.sh ${module.primary_pool.*.rack}" }

Upgrade plan (4-phase, low-risk):
Phase 0 — Prep (2 weeks):
- Finalize procurement for mixed GPU types (order lead times 6-10 weeks).
- Lock TF module changes behind a feature-flagged branch; run full CI on staging hardware.
- BlueHarbor to provision initial HSM stub credentials for integration testing (no secrets yet).

Phase 1 — Baseline deploy (1 week):
- Deploy primary pool with 2 GPUs online and 1 cache node to validate control plane connectivity and service discovery.
- Validate end-to-end requests at low QPS and collect telemetry.

Phase 2 — Scale to steady-state (2 weeks):
- Bring remaining GPUs online, enable autoscaling window, and run load tests.
- Switch traffic gradually with canary route (10 -> 30 -> 60 -> 100%). Monitor p95/p99, token cost, and error rates.

Phase 3 — Hardening and HSM enablement (1 week):
- Enable HSM KMS if customer provisions hardware. Run certificate rotation tests and audit log exports.
- Finalize network ACLs and automated failover to fallback_pool if p99 breaches target.

Q&A and unresolved items (needs answers from BlueHarbor):
- Q1: Can BlueHarbor commit to expanding two constrained racks to full 63A PDUs within 6 months? If not, we must re-scope GPU mix.
- Q2: Are we allowed to terminate TLS on the Redwood control plane endpoints (recommended) or must we route through their HA proxy? Impact: certificate rotation complexity and observability telemetry sampling.
- Q3: What is procurement SLA for HSM delivery? If HSM is delayed beyond Q3, we need a temporary KMS fallback plan.

Risk table (high-level):
- Power limits in racks — mitigation: use mixed GPU types and staggered scheduling, implement power-aware placement in TF modules.
- Network saturation during model warmup — mitigation: KV prefix caching nodes and initial warmup pod strategies + burst pacing.
- HSM unavailability — mitigation: audited software KMS with explicit rotation policy and additional logging for compliance until HSM arrives.

Operational runbook excerpts (quick wins):
- Daily: check PDU draw using scripts/pdu-read.sh and compare to expected-per-GPU table. Threshold alert at 80% of PDU rating.
- On p99 breach: automated traffic-shift to fallback_pool, create incident ticket with stack traces and CPU/GPU temperatures.
- Upgrade window policy: prefer UTC 02:00-05:00 local maintenance window; apply kernel/runtime updates in Canary nodes first.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- [Ava] Draft PR for TF module changes (feature branch). ETA: 2025-02-10.
- [Ravi] Run power validation script on-site and return PDU serials. ETA: 2025-01-21.
- [BlueHarbor infra] Confirm HSM procurement timeline and rack upgrade plan. ETA: 2025-02-07.
- [Mariana] Prepare canary test plan and load scripts for 13B/7B mixes. ETA: 2025-02-17.

Appendix A — quick network topology (text):
- BlueHarbor edge site: 2 x ToR switches (LACP 10Gb each) -> MPLS termination -> Central DC
- VLANs: 210 (control plane), 211 (inference traffic), 212 (management), 213 (observability)
- Suggested firewall rule summary: allow outbound 443 to redwood-control.*; restrict inbound to management VLAN from corporate VPN only.

Appendix B — bench and cost notes (summary):
- Measured token/sec numbers (internal test harness V0.9) used to derive GPU counts. Link to bench spreadsheet in linked_artifacts.
- Estimated monthly infra-only spend (steady-state): approximately $XXk — placeholder until procurement quotes arrive.

This doc is intentionally terse in some sections to accelerate review cycles. Please add inline comments in PR or drop questions into #blueharbor-onprem channel. Next sync call proposed: 2025-02-05 15:00 PST.
